q: Proteins are natural polymers whose monomer units are:
x: Proteins are polyamides built from α-amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Monosaccharides build polysaccharides and nucleotides build nucleic acids.

q: 180 g of glucose is completely fermented by zymase. The maximum mass of ethanol formed is (C 12, H 1, O 16):
x: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. 180 g is 1 mol of glucose, giving 2 mol ethanol = 2 × 46 = 92 g. 88 g is the mass of CO₂, and 46 g uses a 1 : 1 ratio.

q: Polythene (polyethene) is made by polymerising:
x: Polythene is an addition polymer of ethene, CH₂=CH₂: n CH₂=CH₂ → (–CH₂–CH₂–)ₙ. Ethane has no double bond, so it cannot undergo addition polymerisation.

q: The linkage that joins amino acid units in a protein is:
x: The peptide (amide) linkage –CO–NH– forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next. –CO–O– is an ester link and –O– is the glycosidic link of carbohydrates.

q: Which statement about addition polymers is correct?
o: A small molecule such as water is lost at each link
The polymer has the same empirical formula as its monomer
The monomers must have two different functional groups
Only aromatic compounds can act as monomers
x: In addition polymerisation, monomers with C=C bonds join without losing any atoms, so the polymer has the same empirical formula as the monomer. Loss of a small molecule happens in condensation polymerisation.

q: Formation of a peptide bond between two amino acids is a condensation reaction because:
o: A molecule of water is eliminated
The two molecules simply add together
x: The –COOH of one amino acid reacts with the –NH₂ of another, losing H₂O and forming –CO–NH–. Joining with loss of a small molecule is condensation.

q: The monomer of PVC is:
x: PVC, polyvinyl chloride, is made from vinyl chloride (chloroethene), CH₂=CHCl. CF₂=CF₂ gives Teflon and CH₂=CHCH₃ gives polypropene.

q: A single unbranched polypeptide chain contains 60 amino acid units. How many water molecules were eliminated in forming it?
x: Each peptide bond releases one water molecule, and a chain of n amino acids has n − 1 peptide bonds. So 60 − 1 = 59 water molecules are eliminated.

q: Teflon, used to coat non-stick cooking pans, is made by polymerising:
x: Teflon is polytetrafluoroethene, an addition polymer of CF₂=CF₂. Its strong C–F bonds make it chemically inert and heat-resistant. Chloroethene gives PVC and phenylethene gives polystyrene.

q: The primary structure of a protein is:
o: The sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain
The coiling of the chain into an α-helix
The folding of the chain into a three-dimensional shape
The association of several polypeptide chains
x: Primary structure is the order of amino acids, held by peptide bonds. Coiling is secondary, overall folding is tertiary, and the joining of several chains is quaternary structure.

q: Nylon-6,6 is made from:
x: The –NH₂ groups of the diamine react with the –COOH groups of adipic acid, losing water and forming amide links. Ethane-1,2-diol with terephthalic acid gives a polyester, and phenol with methanal gives Bakelite.

q: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet of proteins are mainly held in shape by:
o: Hydrogen bonds between C=O and N–H groups of the peptide backbone
x: Secondary structure is stabilised by hydrogen bonds between the C=O of one peptide group and the N–H of another. Disulphide bridges and ionic attractions between side chains mainly hold the tertiary structure.

q: A sample of polystyrene (monomer C₆H₅CH=CH₂, 104 g mol⁻¹) has an average molar mass of 52 000 g mol⁻¹. About how many monomer units does an average chain contain?
x: Addition polymerisation loses no atoms, so the number of units = 52 000 ÷ 104 = 500. Using 52 for the monomer (half its molar mass) gives 1000, and slipping a power of ten gives 50 or 5000.

q: The repeat unit –CH₂–CH(CN)– is found in an addition polymer made from:
x: Opening the C=C bond of propenenitrile (acrylonitrile) gives –CH₂–CH(CN)–; the polymer is polyacrylonitrile, an acrylic fibre. Propanenitrile has no C=C, so it cannot undergo addition polymerisation, and NC–CH=CH–CN would put a CN group on both carbons.

q: Ethane-1,2-diol (62 g mol⁻¹) and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (166 g mol⁻¹) form the polyester Terylene. What is the molar mass of its repeat unit, –OCH₂CH₂O–CO–C₆H₄–CO–?
x: Each repeat unit comes from one diol and one diacid joined by two ester links, so two H₂O are lost: 62 + 166 − 36 = 192 (check: C₁₀H₈O₄ = 120 + 8 + 64). Forgetting the water gives 228, and removing only one water gives 210.

q: Natural rubber is an addition polymer of:
x: Natural rubber is cis-polyisoprene, built from 2-methylbuta-1,3-diene units. Buta-1,3-diene and chloroprene give synthetic rubbers (polybutadiene and neoprene), and styrene gives polystyrene.

q: Fructose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is classified as:
x: Fructose has six carbon atoms and, in its open-chain form, a ketone group at carbon 2, so it is a ketohexose. Its isomer glucose, with an aldehyde group, is the aldohexose.

q: Which of these disaccharides does NOT reduce Fehling's solution?
x: In sucrose the glycosidic bond joins C-1 of glucose to C-2 of fructose, so neither unit has a free carbonyl group that can open up and be oxidised. Maltose, lactose and cellobiose each keep one free anomeric carbon and are reducing sugars.

q: 34.2 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁, 342 g mol⁻¹) is completely hydrolysed by dilute acid. What total mass of monosaccharides is formed? (C₆H₁₂O₆ = 180 g mol⁻¹)
x: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose). 0.1 mol sucrose gives 0.2 mol hexose = 36.0 g; the extra 1.8 g is the water taken up. 34.2 g ignores that water, and 18.0 g counts glucose only.

q: Humans can digest starch but not cellulose, although both are polymers of glucose. This is because:
o: Cellulose has β-1,4 glycosidic links, which human enzymes cannot hydrolyse
Cellulose is a polymer of fructose units
Starch has β-1,4 links and cellulose has α-1,4 links
Cellulose chains are branched, while starch is unbranched
x: Starch has α-glycosidic links that amylase can hydrolyse; cellulose has β-1,4 links and humans have no cellulase. Swapping α and β is the common slip; cellulose is in fact unbranched, while the amylopectin in starch is branched.

q: Which of these fatty acids is unsaturated?
x: A saturated fatty acid has the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH: C₁₇H₃₅, C₁₅H₃₁ and C₁₁H₂₃ all fit (stearic, palmitic and lauric acids). C₁₇H₃₃COOH has two hydrogens fewer than C₁₇H₃₅COOH, so it has one C=C bond (oleic acid).

q: Glyceryl tristearate (890 g mol⁻¹) is boiled with excess NaOH solution. What mass of NaOH (40 g mol⁻¹) is used up in saponifying 89 g of this fat?
x: A triglyceride has three ester groups: fat + 3NaOH → glycerol + 3 sodium stearate. 89 g is 0.1 mol, which needs 0.3 mol NaOH = 12 g. Using a 1 : 1 ratio gives 4.0 g.

q: Vegetable ghee (banaspati) is made from vegetable oil by:
x: H₂ adds across the C=C bonds of the unsaturated fatty acid chains (Ni catalyst, about 150–200 °C), raising the melting point so the oil becomes a solid fat. Hydrolysis with NaOH would make soap instead.

q: The rate of a typical enzyme-catalysed reaction in the human body falls sharply when the temperature is raised well above about 45 °C. The main reason is that:
o: The substrate molecules move more slowly
The activation energy of the reaction increases
The enzyme is denatured and its active site loses its shape
The enzyme is used up as a reactant
x: Heat breaks the hydrogen bonds and other weak forces that hold the enzyme's three-dimensional shape, so the active site no longer fits the substrate. Molecules move faster, not slower, when heated, and an enzyme is a catalyst, so it is not used up.

q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 30% of the bases are adenine. What percentage of the bases are cytosine?
x: A pairs with T and G pairs with C, so T = 30% and A + T = 60%. Then G + C = 40%, with G = C = 20%. 30% wrongly pairs C with A, and 40% forgets to split G + C equally.
